symptom: Four `mxcli exec` processes creating one entity each on one project in parallel all failed ('disk I/O error (5898)', 'replaced on disk while unwritten changes were held', a temp-file rename error) and rolled back. Measured here (11.12.6 blank project, 8 parallel scripts of 2 entities + 1 association each, 3 rounds): every process exited 0 and the project held 10, 14 and 14 of the 16 entities — updates lost with success reported.
file: internal/projectlock/lock.go Acquire / BusyError; cmd/mxcli/project_write_lock.go programWritesModel / acquireProjectWriteLock (exit 75); wired in cmd/mxcli/cmd_exec.go and cmd/mxcli/oneliner.go. Test: internal/projectlock/lock_test.go
cause: A write run is many unit files plus the .mpr index, read at connect and written later, with a rollback that restores backups on failure; nothing serialised two processes, so each wrote over a project the other had changed, or rolled back over it.
insight: **The reported failure was the lucky case: the measured one is a silent lost update.** Four writers in this environment never collided; eight with an association each did, every round, and every process said it succeeded — so the control has to count what landed, not exit codes. The fix is a per-project O_EXCL lock file (.mxcli/write.lock, portable to Windows) held for the whole exec / -c run — not per write, since a failed run's rollback is itself a write — with a 2s heartbeat; a lock whose same-host pid is dead, or whose heartbeat stopped 30s ago, is taken over, so os.Exit paths that skip the deferred release cannot strand the project. The second writer waits up to 60s, then exits 75 (EX_TEMPFAIL) naming the holder. Programs of only show/describe/select/... take no lock. With the lock: 16/16 entities and 8/8 associations in all three rounds, mx check 0 errors. Not locked: the REPL session, and other writing commands (fix widgets, marketplace).
